subject: Wellbridge DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Todd <samuel.todd@wellbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, we put together an initial evidence pack for the DTIA scope and a draft of the UK addendum with two routing options: (A) full onshore-only processing for UK accounts, or (B) hybrid routing where certain non-PHI telemetry is processed in our eu-central region with contractual safeguards.

Attached: Wellbridge_DTIA_evidence_v1.xlsx (inventory + attestation matrix) and a draft redline of the UK addendum.

Questions we hoped you could answer to speed approvals from your side:
- Is Wellbridge comfortable with hybrid routing for logging and telemetry (non-customer content)?
- Do you require explicit subprocessor notices for the logging pipeline (we currently use managed Kafka + S3 in eu-central and a CDN in eu-west)?
- Any additional evidence items your compliance team needs (network diagrams, penetration test reports, SOC 2 extracts)?

If it helps, I can loop in our infra lead Kim to run through the network map and data residency guarantees. Proposed next step: quick 30-min working session with your security contact + our infra/legal this week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Wellbridge_DTIA_evidence_v1.xlsx, UK_Addendum_draft_redlines.docx

From: Samuel Todd <samuel.todd@wellbridgehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ross <anna.ross@lawfirm-lyons.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination

Naomi —

Thanks, received. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side:

1) Hybrid routing: acceptable in principle for non-customer-content telemetry but we need an explicit list of telemetry fields that could be processed outside the UK. We also need a contractual assurance (TIA/DTIA clause) that telemetry will never contain patient-identifiable fields.

2) Subprocessors: please provide the subprocessor list for the logging pipeline (managed Kafka vendor, S3 storage, CDN provider). We will need vendor-level control descriptions (encryption in transit/at rest, access controls) for each.

3) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and most recent penetration test summary would be helpful. If SOC 2 is redacted, a summary with scope is fine.

Anna (cc) will review the draft UK addendum and come back with redlines; can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a UK-only routing fallback if a local regulator requires it?

We can do a 30-min session on Thu 14th 10:00-10:30 UK time — will that work?

Regards,
Sam
Director, Security & Compliance — Wellbridge Health

Attachments referenced: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Todd <samuel.todd@wellbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination

Sam —

Great — Thu 14th 10:00 UK works. Quick replies inline below and attaching a network map PDF that shows the kafka/s3/cdn topology.

- Hybrid telemetry fields: kim will produce a one-pager enumerating the telemetry fields we might process outside the UK and confirm none contain PHI. We will map each field to vendor and retention window.
- Subprocessors: current logging pipeline subprocessors: Confluent (managed Kafka), AWS (S3 in eu-central-1), FastEdge CDN (eu-west edge nodes). We will provide vendor control matrices and indicate where customer-data is logically separated.
- Evidence: Laura will share the SOC 2 executive summary and a pen test summary (redacted) for the relevant infra scope.
- UK-only fallback: Vivek — can you confirm feasibility and expected lead time for an onshore-only routing fallback (i.e., failover to UK region endpoints and key segregation)?

Next steps:
1) Kim to deliver telemetry field list and network_map.pdf (attached) by EOD Thu (14th).
2) Laura to push SOC 2 exec summary + pen test summary by Fri.
3) Internal meeting Thu 14th 10:00 UK / 05:00 PT.

Naomi

Attachments: network_map.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Todd <samuel.todd@wellbridgehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ross <anna.ross@lawfirm-lyons.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination

Sam/Anna —

Anna, thanks for starting the review. Quick flags from legal based on initial read of your redlines:

- We can accept a UK Addendum that limits cross-border transfers for customer content, but we need carveouts for operational telemetry (as discussed). Those carveouts will be enumerated in the schedule.
- We propose a fallback SLA: Redwood will support a configurable UK-only routing mode that can be activated within 30 business days following written notice and onboarding of any required subprocessors in the UK. (We cannot commit to instantaneous cutovers due to data migration and key material separation.)
- Regarding the TIA language: we will include a clause requiring Redwood to maintain technical and organizational measures for telemetry segregation and to provide annual attestation.

I've attached the SOC 2 executive summary and a redacted pentest summary. Please confirm if that's sufficient or if you need the full reports under an NDA.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_exec_summary.pdf, pentest_redacted_summary.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Todd <samuel.todd@wellbridgehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jan 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DTIA evidence + UK addendum routing coordination

Sam —

Following the working session and the evidence ask, quick technical summary and proposed controls we can include in the TIA schedule:

- Telemetry field inventory: attached in the spreadsheet. Fields flagged as "sensitive" are excluded from hybrid routing. Everything else can be processed in eu-central with pseudonymization applied at ingress.
- Subprocessor controls: Confluent (eu kafka) supports customer-managed encryption keys; AWS S3 buckets used for logs will have SSE-KMS with keys scoped per-customer. FastEdge CDN caches are configured not to persist request bodies for log-forwarding paths.
- UK fallback: implementation plan — spin up UK-region Kafka/S3 with key segregation and db migration tooling. Estimated lead time: 18 business days once commercial commitment is approved. We recommend including a 30-business day SLA in the addendum to be conservative.

Action items for Wellbridge: confirm the list of specific telemetry fields you want classified as "always-UK" and sign off on the proposed 30-business day fallback SLA. Once we have that we can finalize the addendum and move to signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Wellbridge_DTIA_evidence_v1.xlsx (updated)
